context: A uni student interviews a retired political journalist
purpose: Teach: 安倍/福田/中川/藤田/一郎/仁/隆/剛

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間いただきありがとうございます。まず、安倍元首相を取材された頃の話を伺えますか。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. First, could you tell me about when you covered former Prime Minister Abe?
lines.style: Polite respectful tone, slightly nervous but professional young interviewer

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、あの頃はね、福田元総理や中川氏ともよく話したよ。みんな個性の強い政治家でね。
lines.en: Ah, back then I often spoke with former PM Fukuda and Mr. Nakagawa too. They were all politicians with strong personalities.
lines.style: Warm reminiscent elder voice, slow paced with fond nostalgia

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 当時、特に印象に残っている論点は何でしたか。共謀罪の議論などは特に厳密な取材が求められたと思いますが。
lines.en: What issues stand out most from that time? I imagine the conspiracy law debate especially demanded rigorous reporting.
lines.style: Earnest student tone, focused single question with academic precision

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうだね、共謀罪は厳密な裏取りが要った。国民主権の根幹に関わる話だからね。同時期に政教分離の判例も追っていたよ。
lines.en: Yes, the conspiracy law required strict verification. It touched the very heart of popular sovereignty. I was also tracking separation-of-church-and-state rulings around the same time.
lines.style: Thoughtful elderly statesman tone, weighty and reflective delivery

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 外交面ではいかがでしたか。五カ国会議の取材もされたと伺いました。
lines.en: What about on the diplomatic side? I heard you also covered the five-nation conference.
lines.style: Curious follow-up question, leaning forward with genuine interest

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ええ、あの会議では人種差別や道徳教育まで議題に上ってね。まさしく時代の転換点だった。地方では鹿児島県、石川県、長野県にも足を運んだよ。
lines.en: Yes, even racial discrimination and moral education came up at that conference. It was truly a turning point. On the regional side, I traveled to Kagoshima, Ishikawa, and Nagano too.
lines.style: Storytelling grandfatherly cadence, weighty recall with vivid detail

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 先生がお書きになった岩波新書も拝読しました。学園紛争の章が特に印象的でした。当時は東京大学卒業の若手と組まれていたとか。
lines.en: I also read the Iwanami paperback you wrote — the chapter on the campus protests was especially striking. I gather you partnered with a young Tokyo University graduate back then.
lines.style: Admiring student tone, citing the book respectfully with genuine interest

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 光栄だね。藤田さんという先輩と、川崎市から郡山まで一緒に回ったよ。農林水産省の地方支局にも何度も通ったね。
lines.en: I'm honored. A senior named Fujita and I traveled together from Kawasaki City all the way to Koriyama. We visited regional bureaus of the Ministry of Agriculture many times.
lines.style: Warm storytelling elder voice, recalling a mentor with affection

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 同期の山田一郎も忘れられない男でね。仁愛の人だった。隆さんや剛さんも、もう鬼籍に入ったよ。
lines.en: My colleague Yamada Ichiro was also unforgettable — a man of true benevolence. Mr. Takashi and Mr. Tsuyoshi are gone now too.
lines.style: Melancholic elder voice, quiet pause between names with emotion

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 最後に、若い世代に強く推奨されることは何でしょうか。アフリカ南部の紛争報道などにも関心があります。
lines.en: Finally, what would you strongly recommend to the younger generation? I'm also interested in reporting on conflicts in southern Africa.
lines.style: Closing interview question, respectful and measured tone
